rulings.matter: 1 -- are RUL-0004's five blocking conditions discharged
rulings.ruling:
FOUR ARE DISCHARGED. ONE IS NOT, AND IT IS NOT DISCHARGED IN THE SPECIFIC WAY ITS AUTHOR WROTE IT TO EXCLUDE.

(1) CRITERION 11 T0 RECORD -- DISCHARGED, AND IT IS THE BEST EVIDENCE RECORD THIS STUDIO HAS PRODUCED. Studio/evidence/tests/EVD-0008.json: tier T0, taskId WO-0009, commit 704dc4e, producedBy core-simulation-engineer. It inlines genuine NUnit output -- 'Failed Criterion11_RejectedRegisterKillDoesNotLeaveKillsIncrementedAcrossTheThrow [1 ms] Expected: 1 But was: 2' and three siblings -- in NUnit's own two-part idiom, which is precisely the tell RUL-0004 matter 2b used to catch the markdown as a reconstruction. It names the predicted set of four and reports exactly four reddened. And its summary does something I want recorded as a precedent: it explains its own verdict field, 'pass because the demonstration did what it was required to do, not because the code under it was sound'. A T0 record whose verdict means the opposite of what a casual reader assumes is a trap the studio will otherwise walk into, and this record disarmed it in one clause.

(2) THE MARKDOWN LEAVES THE EVIDENCE TREE -- DISCHARGED. Studio/evidence now contains only EVD-0001 through EVD-0011 plus metrics_pre.json and metrics_post.json. There is no markdown file anywhere under it. RUL-0004 permitted deletion once the content was inside a governed record, and the content is: EVD-0008 carries the same substance, with a commit, a producer, a timestamp and captured rather than composed output. The prose that read as authoritative while escaping every check on records is gone.

(3) CRITERION 13 T1 RECORD -- DISCHARGED AS A RECORD. EVD-0009.json: tier T1, taskId WO-0009, commit 704dc4e, buildWarnings 0, coreTests 180, kernelTests 149, gate-g2.sh green. See matter 3 for a caveat about which tree it covers, which does not un-discharge the condition but does bear on closure.

(4) CRITERION 13 SECOND CLAUSE, THE DIFF -- NOT DISCHARGED. See matter 4.

(5) Criterion5_UniversalTest_ManyDifferentValidScoreValues AMENDED -- DISCHARGED, EXACTLY AND WITH ONE IMPROVEMENT ON THE RULING THAT ORDERED IT. Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WO0009CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:300-322 now reads `{ 0, 1, 5, 10, 100, 1000, int.MaxValue / 2, int.MaxValue / 4 }`. One array element changed, in one test, which is the whole of what RUL-0004 authorised and nothing beyond it. The comment states the sequence is 'deliberately kept inside int range ... because Score overflow is an open question, not certified behaviour' and points at Criterion5_BoundaryTest_LargeScoreValue as retaining int.MaxValue coverage without wraparound. That is the substance of the direction, not a gesture at it. The passing assertion that Score may accumulate to a negative number is gone; coverage is not reduced and no assertion is weakened.

AND THE ARITHMETIC, WHICH I CHECKED RATHER THAN COPIED, BECAUSE THE ONE THING EVERYONE IN THIS CHAIN GOT WRONG WAS COPYING IT. RUL-0004 directed the amendment and stated the resulting sum as 1,610,614,850, and the plan dispatched to me repeated that figure by transcription. Computing it: 0 + 1 + 5 + 10 + 100 + 1000 = 1,116; int.MaxValue / 2 = 1,073,741,823; int.MaxValue / 4 = 536,870,911; total 1,610,613,850. The ruling's figure is high by exactly 1,000. The comment the implementing agent actually wrote says 1,610,613,850 -- the correct value. So the agent computed the sum instead of copying it out of the ruling that told it what to do, and quietly got it right where two directors above it got it wrong. That is worth more than the thousand it corrects: it is the difference between an agent executing an instruction and an agent checking one. I record it as credit.

rulings.matter: 2 -- criterion 5 read absolutely or relatively, ruled independently rather than inherited
rulings.ruling:
THE RELATIVE READING GOVERNS. I reach qa-director's conclusion and I did not reach it by adopting qa-director's reasoning, because I was asked not to and because an adjudicator who inherits the reading he is meant to review has reviewed nothing. I give two grounds, the second of which RUL-0004 does not contain and which I think is the stronger.

FIRST, THE GRAMMATICAL GROUND, which is qa-director's and which I have checked and endorse. The criterion reads: 'For every valid (non-negative) scoreValue, RegisterKill's observable behaviour is unchanged from today: Kills increases by exactly 1 and Score increases by exactly scoreValue, in the same run, for the same sequence of calls, as before this fix.' The main clause asserts a COMPARISON -- 'unchanged from today'. The colon introduces an expansion of what unchanged means, and the sentence closes 'as before this fix'. The criterion anchors itself to pre-fix behaviour twice, at both ends. To read 'Score increases by exactly scoreValue' as a free-standing absolute claim about int arithmetic, one has to treat both anchors as decoration. A reading that renders half its own sentence dead text is the worse reading of the two, and there is no third.

SECOND, THE GROUND FROM WHAT THE CRITERION IS FOR, which I did not find in RUL-0004 and which I find decisive on its own. WO-0009 is an ORDERING fix. Its entire subject is when validation runs relative to mutation. Acceptance criteria exist to discriminate a correct delivery of THIS order from an incorrect one. Under the absolute reading, criterion 5 asserts that Score never wraps -- a property this fix does not touch, cannot introduce and cannot repair, and which is false identically before and after. It would therefore be failed equally by the pre-fix code, the post-fix code, and every possible implementation that stores Score in an int. A criterion that every candidate delivery fails identically discriminates nothing and cannot do the job a criterion is there to do. Under the relative reading it discriminates precisely: it rules out an implementation whose new validation branch alters behaviour for some non-negative input. That is exactly the failure mode this order could plausibly have introduced, and it is the one the criterion is positioned to catch.

So the relative reading is not the charitable reading; it is the only one on which the criterion functions. On it, criterion 5 is SATISFIED, and satisfied by inspection rather than by sampling: the added branch is unreachable for any non-negative scoreValue and nothing else in the method changed, so no non-negative input can behave differently than it did before. Overflow is identical either side of the fix.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS, stated so the ruling is falsifiable rather than merely confident. If work-order-author confirms it intended the absolute reading, then criterion 5 is false against every int-backed implementation, it becomes unsatisfiableAsWritten, the criterion is its author's to amend and not mine, and WO-0009 does not close until it is amended. The author is the only party who can settle that and has not been asked. I am not asking, because a criterion whose only coherent reading is the relative one does not become ambiguous merely because a second reading can be written down.

I ALSO RECORD WHAT I DECLINED TO DO. Refusing closure on criterion 5 was offered to me as an available ground and it would have been a comfortable one: it would have made my refusal turn on someone else's specification rather than on the studio's own missing machinery, which is a softer thing to say. I refuse closure on other grounds and I want it clear that criterion 5 is not among them.

rulings.matter: 3 -- which tree the T1 evidence actually covers
rulings.ruling:
NO RECORD IN THE TREE DEMONSTRABLY COVERS A GREEN SUITE ON A TREE CONTAINING THE AMENDMENT RUL-0004 ORDERED, AND I STATE THE ASSUMPTION THIS RESTS ON BECAUSE IT IS WEAKER THAN MY OTHER FINDINGS.

On the records' own timestamps: EVD-0008 and EVD-0009 are stamped 2026-08-30T01:18:16Z at commit 704dc4e. EVD-0010 and EVD-0011 are stamped 2026-08-30T07:50:49Z at commit 4f4135e. RUL-0004, the ruling that AUTHORISED the Criterion5 amendment, is stamped 2026-08-30T09:00:00Z. Every evidence record in the tree therefore predates, on its own stamp, the authorisation for a change that is in the working tree today. If those stamps are accurate, no recorded build-and-suite run has ever executed the amended Criterion5_UniversalTest_ManyDifferentValidScoreValues.

I weigh this carefully rather than pressing it. The amendment changes one array element and cannot alter a test count, so the coreTests figure of 180 in both T1 records is consistent with either tree and discriminates nothing. The change is very unlikely to break anything -- the amended sequence sums to 1,610,613,850, comfortably inside int range, which is the entire point of it. And I have no independent clock; if the 'at' fields are nominal rather than captured, the ordering I have inferred does not hold and this observation collapses.

But the reason this is worth writing down is not the risk that the test fails. It is that this is precisely the question the evidence schema's commit requirement exists to answer, and today it cannot be answered from the record. The proposed closure cites a G2 run at commit 13900d3 which is said to carry all of this -- and if that run were recorded as a gate verdict with its commit, this matter would be settled in one line rather than reasoned about from timestamps. It is another instance of the same gap, arriving from a different direction, and it is discharged by the same single artefact.

NO, ON TWO GROUNDS, THE FIRST OF WHICH IS COMMON TO BOTH ORDERS AND SUFFICIENT ALONE.

GROUND ONE -- NO GATE VERDICT EXISTS. The full reasoning is in RUL-0005 matter 2 and I will not restate it at length here: gate.schema.json defines gate-verdict as a record keyed to a taskId; no live instance exists anywhere in this studio for any order; the only occurrences of the string in the repository are the schema and four kernel fixtures. I have no shell, no git and no CI access, the strings '13900d3' and 'run 58' appear nowhere in the repository, and my only route to the claimed gate result is the word of the agent that dispatched me. Writing completedByGate 'G2' on that basis records that a gate said so when in fact an agent said so and an adjudicator wrote it down. G2's owner is 'ci' and its overridableBy is empty by schema; the verdict is not mine to supply. What closes this is small and specific: a gate-verdict record, gate 'G2', taskId 'WO-0009', verdict 'pass', evaluatedBy 'ci', evidence ['EVD-0008','EVD-0009'], with its commit.

GROUND TWO -- CRITERION 13'S SECOND CLAUSE IS UNMET, AND THIS ONE IS SPECIFIC TO WO-0009. Criterion 13 requires the suite to build and pass 'with no assertion in any existing test file altered, weakened or removed'. That second clause is part of the criterion's own text, not a director's addition, and RUL-0004 made it a blocking condition in those terms: someone with a shell must diff Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateTests.cs, RunStateVerificationTests.cs and WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs and confirm the five tests named by criteria 6, 7 and 9 are untouched.

I searched for it. There is no such record. I grepped Studio/evidence for 'diff', 'untouched' and 'unchanged' and the only match is an unrelated line in EVD-0007; I grepped the whole of Studio for 'git diff' and the file names, and the only hits are the orders, the rulings, two proposals, one report and two build scripts -- the instructions to do it, never the result. RUL-0004 anticipated exactly this and wrote the condition to exclude the cheap discharge: 'I read them as intact; reading is not diffing.' I have now read them as intact too. That gets the studio no further than qa-director already got, and clearing the condition by doing again the thing its author said was insufficient would be the emptiest possible form of adjudication.

I RECORD WHAT IS MECHANICALLY COVERED, so the condition is not read as broader than it is. Studio/build/check-forbidden-remedies.sh check 3 counts Assert./Assume. occurrences per file against the merge base and fails the gate if any file lost one, and gate-g2.sh runs it. If a G2 run is green then no file under Assets/Tests LOST an assertion. So 'removed' is covered mechanically; 'altered' and 'weakened' are not, because an assertion whose expected value was changed keeps its count exactly. Roughly a third of the clause is covered and the diff is needed for the rest.

ONE COMPLICATION FOR WHOEVER PERFORMS IT, so it is not discovered at the last moment. RUL-0004's condition says the only change in the round should be the added WO0009CriteriaVerificationTests.cs. That is no longer literally true and is not supposed to be: WO0009CriteriaVerificationTests.cs has since been amended under RUL-0004 matter 3's own authorisation, and WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs has since been rewritten in one test under RUL-0001 matter 2's. The diff must therefore be read against those two authorisations rather than against a blanket expectation of no change, and it must confirm that nothing OUTSIDE them moved. That is a judgement, not a mechanical comparison, and it is why the output belongs in an evidence record where the next reader can weigh it rather than in an agent's summary sentence.

AS WITH WO-0008, NEITHER GROUND IS A FINDING AGAINST THE DELIVERY. The fix is correct, RUL-0004 found no criterion violated, and every condition that was about the code has been met. What is missing is a verification step nobody ran and a record nobody has ever had to create. The order is finished; the studio cannot yet say so.

criteriaAssessment.notes: Criteria 1-10 and 12 are ADOPTED from RUL-0004 and not independently re-derived, with one exception. RUL-0004 graded them by reading Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs as delivered, nothing in this round changed that file, and re-grading eleven criteria I have no new information about would be cost without information. The exception is criterion 5, which I was specifically asked not to inherit and did not: matter 2 rules the relative reading governs, on the grammatical ground RUL-0004 gave and on a second, independent ground about what an acceptance criterion is for that RUL-0004 does not contain. I record, as RUL-0004 did, that criterion 5's delegation clause -- the fix must not duplicate Score-mutation logic outside AddScore -- holds by INSPECTION ONLY and that no test can reach it through a sealed type's public API, and that the verifier's comment implying otherwise must not be carried into the gate packet. Criterion 11 moves to satisfiedByEvidence on EVD-0008, which is what RUL-0004 asked for and did not have. Criterion 13 stays notYetEvidenced, and I want the split stated precisely rather than left as a bare grade: its FIRST clause, that the full suite builds and passes, is evidenced by EVD-0009 and I treat it as met, subject to the caveat in matter 3 about which tree that run covered. Its SECOND clause, that no assertion in any existing test file was altered, weakened or removed, is not evidenced anywhere in the repository. check-forbidden-remedies.sh covers 'removed' mechanically and covers neither 'altered' nor 'weakened'. This is an unperformed verification step and not a defect in the code -- the same step is outstanding on WO-0008 and graded there against criterion 8.

blockingConditions: NO GATE VERDICT EXISTS FOR WO-0009. Required to close: a record with kind 'gate-verdict', gate 'G2', taskId 'WO-0009', verdict 'pass', evaluatedBy 'ci', evidence ['EVD-0008','EVD-0009'], an evaluatedAt and the commit evaluated. No live gate-verdict record exists anywhere in this studio for any order; the string occurs only in gate.schema.json and four kernel fixtures. Reasoning in full at RUL-0005 matter 2. G2's owner is 'ci' and its overridableBy is empty by schema; this verdict is neither mine to supply nor my dispatcher's to supply by reporting one.

CRITERION 13 SECOND CLAUSE: run git diff on Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateTests.cs, RunStateVerificationTests.cs and WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs and record the output as evidence. Confirm the five tests named by criteria 6, 7 and 9 are untouched, and that the only changes outside them are the two authorised ones -- the Criterion5 array element under RUL-0004 matter 3 and Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote under RUL-0001 matter 2. Nothing in the repository records this having been done. RUL-0004 wrote the condition to exclude discharge by reading; I have read the files too and that gets nobody further than qa-director already got.

NO RECORD TIES A GREEN BUILD-AND-SUITE RUN TO A TREE CONTAINING THE RUL-0004-AUTHORISED Criterion5 AMENDMENT. On the records' own timestamps every evidence record predates RUL-0004's authorisation of it. See matter 3, including the assumption this rests on. Recording the gate verdict with its commit discharges this and the first condition together, which is why I have not asked for a separate run.
nonBlockingLogged: Criterion 5's absolute reading is resolved against, in matter 2, on independent grounds. It is not a blocker and should not be reopened as one. If work-order-author states that it intended the absolute reading, that is new information and the criterion becomes its author's to amend; nobody else may amend it and nobody should read this ruling as having done so.

RUL-0004's arithmetic slip -- 1,610,614,850 for a sum that computes to 1,610,613,850 -- is corrected in matter 1 and has no consequence: the implementing agent computed the figure rather than copying it and wrote the correct one into the test's comment. Recorded because the slip propagated through two directors and a dispatch plan by transcription, and because the agent lowest in the chain was the only one who checked.

RegisterKill's throw still duplicates AddScore's message verbatim with nothing asserting they match, and AddScore validates before its IsOver check while RegisterKill checks IsOver first, with nothing in the XML doc saying why two adjacent GameManager passthroughs behave oppositely on the same bad input. Both carried forward unaltered from RUL-0004's non-blocking log. I neither cleared nor promoted either; they are quality's to detect and compose with the message-equality test already directed under WO-0010.

Criterion 12's engine-free clause has now gone three rounds with no test, and RUL-0004's judgement stands unaltered: it is enforced mechanically by MergeSurvivor.Core.Build compiling Assets/Core against netstandard2.1 with no UnityEngine reference and warnings as errors, so the missing test costs less than it looks. Not blocking, and I decline to re-sound an alarm a director has already correctly de-escalated.

PRO-0003 remains status 'open' although WO-0009 was minted from it and is now delivered and adjudicated twice. RUL-0002, RUL-0003 and RUL-0004 each flagged the triage backlog and nothing moved; RUL-0004 matter 5 records the concrete cost, a director at the five-proposal cap unable to file a finding it had already made. Triage priority is mine alone and it goes ahead of new work next period.

Studio/state/project-state.json still lists WO-0009 as 'queued' with no assignee. It is delivered, adjudicated and one artefact from closing. Mine to correct, deliberately not corrected in this pass rather than widening an adjudication into bookkeeping.
WO-0009's recorded status is 'dispatched'; on the facts it is gate_pending. The file is left untouched for the reason given in boundariesObserved.

boundariesObserved: I wrote no production code and no test code and touched nothing under Assets/**. I amended no acceptance criterion: criterion 5 is resolved by a reading recorded here, and I state explicitly that a reading is not an amendment and that if the absolute reading was intended the criterion is its author's to change and nobody else's. I left Studio/orders/open/WO-0009.json byte-for-byte untouched. I was authorised to write status, completedByGate and completedAt if the order was closable; it is not, and the correct action on a refusal is to leave the file exactly as found, including its stale 'dispatched' status, which I have logged rather than quietly improved. I did not mark WO-0009 complete, did not sign G2, and did not treat a reported CI result as a gate verdict. I cleared and weakened none of RUL-0004's five conditions: I found four discharged on the tree and the fifth not discharged, and I declined the available shortcut of clearing it by reading the files, which is the method its author had already ruled insufficient. I did not re-derive the eleven criteria RUL-0004 graded by inspection, except criterion 5 which I was asked to rule on independently and did. I did not modify PRO-0003's status, LESSONS.md, Studio/build, the kernel, the constitution or CI. I filed no challenge and no proposal; the findings that would ordinarily become proposals are gaps in machinery I own, and a ruling plus a digest item is the honest instrument for those rather than a proposal addressed to myself. I did not escalate to the founder. The founder asked that these orders be closed and I am declining; declining a request that falls inside my own authority is not an escalation, and nothing here touches the pillars, the non-goals, an irreversible action, monetisation or player data.
whyNoChallenge: No criterion of WO-0009 is violated by the implementation. RUL-0004 checked all thirteen against the delivered RunState.cs and found the fix does exactly what the order asked -- validation ahead of the increment, behind the IsOver return, with RegisterKill's own ParamName, AddScore untouched, and no observable change for any non-negative input -- and nothing in this round disturbs that. The one criterion I grade unmet, 13, is unmet in its second clause for want of a diff nobody ran, which is a missing verification step and not a defect; challenging an implementer because a director's named gate step went unperformed would be manufactured. Criterion 5's absolute clause is false about int arithmetic but false identically before and after the fix, and matter 2 resolves which reading governs rather than converting a resolvable ambiguity into a challenge. The gate-verdict gap that blocks closure is a hole in the studio's own machinery which I own; filing a challenge against myself would be theatre. The remaining findings from RUL-0004 sit in Assets/Tests, which is quality's own output and quality's own ruling to make.
limitations: I have no shell, no git and no CI access; my instruments were file reading and search over the working tree. Five consequences. First, I could not verify that G2 run 58 exists, that it is green, or that commit 13900d3 exists or carries this work; neither string appears anywhere in the repository, and I have ruled that I cannot check the claim rather than that it is false. Second, I could not perform the criterion 13 diff, which is why it remains a condition rather than being cleared. Third, matter 3's timestamp finding rests on the 'at' fields of the evidence records being captured rather than nominal; I have no independent clock, and if those fields are nominal that observation collapses, though nothing else in this ruling depends on it. Fourth, my grading of criteria 1-4 and 6-12 is adopted from RUL-0004 and inherits whatever that reading was worth; RUL-0004 was itself produced without a shell, so criteria 1, 2 and 3 rest on an inspection corroborated by a revert run that is now, unlike when RUL-0004 was written, properly recorded in EVD-0008. Fifth, I verified the amended array's sum by hand arithmetic rather than by execution: 1,116 + 1,073,741,823 + 536,870,911 = 1,610,613,850, comfortably inside int range. It agrees with the comment the implementer wrote and disagrees with RUL-0004 by exactly 1,000. If execution contradicts me I would rather be told and withdraw than have the difference reconciled.
